summary: Lockfile/manifest-only change to the Rust half of @cipherstash/protect-ffi: pins cipherstash-client, cts-common, stack-auth and stack-profile move =0.42.0 -> =0.42.2, which also moves cipherstash-config, cipherstash-core and zerokms-protocol (0.12.26 -> 0.12.28), and moves stack-auth's jsonwebtoken from 9.3.1 (ring backend) to 10.4.0 (aws-lc-rs backend) to address CVE-2026-25537. No first-party source changes. The material risk is a behaviour change inside the token-handling and encryption crates that this repository cannot see: a stricter JWT major version could reject or mis-handle service tokens and break every encrypt/decrypt call. CI on the head commit is fully green, including the live protect-ffi integration suite, Rust test+clippy (host and wasm32) and the Deno WASM E2E, which covers the happy path. aws-lc-rs was already in the build graph at base (rustls, vitaminc-encrypt), so new native build toolchain risk is small. The changeset is parked as .md.deferred per the documented pre-cutover convention, so nothing publishes from this PR and the CVE fix does not reach npm consumers until the cutover PR.

behaviour_changes.description: stack-auth's JWT library moves across a major version (jsonwebtoken 9.3.1 -> 10.4.0) and switches crypto backend from ring to aws-lc-rs, adding signature, zeroize and getrandom. Any decoding/validation of service-token claims inside stack-auth now runs on the new library, whose claim validation is stricter (the CVE fix concerns nbf/exp type confusion).

Encryption-core crates bumped by patch versions: cipherstash-client/config/core 0.42.0 -> 0.42.2 and zerokms-protocol 0.12.26 -> 0.12.28. Their dependency lists are unchanged in the lockfile; what changed in their code is not visible here and is not described in the PR beyond 'No API changes'.
A patch changeset for @cipherstash/protect-ffi is added under the inert .md.deferred extension, so changeset version/publish ignore it until the publishing cutover PR renames all parked changesets.

failure_scenarios.title: jsonwebtoken 10 handles service-token claims differently, so auth fails or token refresh breaks
failure_scenarios.trigger: stack-auth (via AutoStrategy or a JS-backed strategy) decodes or validates a CTS/OIDC-federated service token whose claims jsonwebtoken 10 treats differently from 9.3.1 (e.g. stricter nbf/exp typing, required-claim defaults, or missing crypto-provider selection on some target), especially at refresh time after the first token expires.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: jsonwebtoken moves across a major version with a new crypto backend (Cargo.lock jsonwebtoken entry at head). stack-auth is its only dependent. protect-ffi obtains every ServiceToken through stack-auth (lib.rs, wasm.rs, client_options.rs). The upstream stack-auth diff 0.42.0 -> 0.42.2 that adapts to the new API could not be read.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Clients fail to obtain or refresh a token, so encrypt/decrypt fails for all users on the affected path (fails loudly, no data corruption). A refresh-only failure would show up only in long-running processes, after the first token expires.

failure_scenarios.title: Release-time platform build of the new graph fails or misbehaves on a target PR CI does not build
failure_scenarios.trigger: The cutover release runs _build-ffi-artifacts.yml for the six platforms (darwin-x64, darwin-arm64, win32-x64-msvc, linux-x64-gnu, linux-arm64-gnu cross, linux-x64-musl) with jsonwebtoken now linking aws-lc-rs.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: PR CI builds only the host and wasm32; the six-platform matrix runs only from release.yml or the manually dispatched ffi-preflight.yml. aws-lc-rs was already compiled at base via rustls/vitaminc-encrypt, so the new edges are jsonwebtoken -> aws-lc-rs and pure-Rust crates, which lowers the likelihood.
failure_scenarios.consequence: The release job fails closed and needs a fix and re-run; or, if one platform build silently differs, a broken binary ships for that platform.
